items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I called both of them -- they were both pretty heavy in to the church, and I told him what we wanted to do, and did they think we could pull it off. And they said yes. So I used 10 musicians and about 35 singers, and we went to Radio Recorders...

ctx.x: But a record came out, "Oh Happy Day" at the time, and so Jay [Flasko] over at Dunhill, he's a great marketing man, and so he saw the marketing people that were doing this record had slipped up on something, and so he called me on a Friday and told me he wanted an album on the street by Monday and could I do it.

He wanted 10 religious songs, but he wanted "Oh Happy Day" in it, and he said he had the cover ready, and could I get the record. And I had him hold on the phone and I got in touch -- incidentally, the young man works here now, James Carmichael, who produces the Commodores -- well, James Carmichael and another fellow named Arthur Wright who is now producing the Pips, well I called both of them -- they were both pretty heavy in to the church, and I told him what we wanted to do, and did they think we could pull it…

So I used 10 musicians and about 35 singers, and we went to Radio Recorders, and one would rehearse the singers and the other would rehearse the band. And I had 3 copies over in the corner; they were copying the music as we did it. And now what he had detected, that they had Edwin Hawkins -- it said the Edwin Hawkins Singers on their album; you know, the people who did "Oh Happy Day" -- so all he had on his was "Oh Happy Day".
